page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Seb Lime
title: Seb Lime
topic: Language for talking on he phone
description:
Anna has been told to improve her telephone manner and has welcomed some friendly and useful advice from Denise. They practise some mock phone conversations but Anna receives a real call with a request of a personal nature. How is Anna going to respond? Will her telephone manner be up to the challenge?
This episode focuses on how to talk to a business client on the phone.
phrases: Hello? Tip Top Trading. This is Anna speaking.
Hello Mrs Smith, how can I help you?
Hello Mrs Smith, how are you?
I'm really sorry, he's not available at the moment. Can I take a message?
I'm afraid he's busy - shall I ask him to call you back?

listening_challenge.question: What does Seb Lime want Anna to do?
listening_challenge.answer: To go for lunch with him.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: (answering the phone) Yes?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Stop! That's all wrong. I'm going to call you again. This time…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello. Here we are in the middle of a telephone training session with Denise and Anna. What fun!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
…this time, you don't say 'yes' when you answer, it's rude. Call me and I'll show you how it's done.
(sound of 4-digit dialling, then phone rings)
Hello? Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Wow, that’s good.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
And, you can say your name. Hello? Tip Top Trading. Denise speaking. Try it.
(dialling, then ring)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello? Tip Top Trading. Denise speaking.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Say: "Anna speaking!"

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, sorry, I'm so stressed by all this. Hello Anna speaking.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You sound like you're sitting on a pineapple. Listen to my voice: Hello? Denise speaking.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello? Anna speaking.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Good. Now, when the person has introduced themself – this is Mrs Smith or whatever, say: Hello Mrs Smith, how can I help you? Or, if you know them already, you might say: Hello Mrs Smith, how are you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay, what if Mrs Smith wants to speak to Tom but he's not there?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You say: "I'm really sorry, he's not available at the moment. Can I take a message?" Or: "I'm afraid he's busy, shall I ask him to call you back?"

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
And, to end a conversation, you can say: "Thank you for calling, goodbye." Let's do another practice!
(phone rings)

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello? Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hello, this is Mrs Smith.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello Mrs Smith, how can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I'd like to speak to Tom please.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm really sorry, he's not available at the moment. Can I take a message?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's okay, I'll try again later.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay. Thank you for calling, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
Excellent!
(phone rings)
Oh!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: How did you call me without dialling?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I didn't, that's a real call!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no, I'm all nervous now. Hello? Tip Top Trading. This is Anna speaking.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Hello Anna, this is Seb Lime.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sublime?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Mr Lime from Citrus Ventures. But I think we should be on first name terms now, so call me Seb.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay, er, Seb. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: I just wanted to say again that your Imperial Lemon is fantastic... and I was wondering if you'd like to do lunch with me sometime?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Lunch? Er...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I knew it! Mr Lime is interested in more than just your lemons!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Would you like to discuss the Imperial Lemon?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Forget the lemons Anna! The reason I want to see you is more of a personal nature.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Personnel? Er... Can I call you back? I'm afraid I'm a bit busy at the moment...

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: …bbbut…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well Anna! Mr Lime eh?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear Denise, I think I need a bit more help from you. He wants to talk about personnel…people, staffing…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Are you sure? I think he means a personal nature, not personnel! That Mr Lime!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Mr Lime indeed. Anyway, Anna had an excellent phone manner. Let's hear those phrases again:
But how is Anna going to handle Mr Lime's request? I can't wait till next time! Bye!
